newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds soared on Friday, caught up in a surge in European bond markets after German Bund futures set a new contract high.
The 10-year yield dropped to 5.57 percent, the lowest level since January 1994, from 5.68 percent as buyers scrambled to get scarce guilder paper from very few willing sellers.
"It's like a buying panic. Everbody is buying at the same time. That's the reason the market is going up so fast," said one fixed interest trader.
He attributed the strength to strong institutional liquidity and a view that interest rates would continue falling.
Bund futures earlier broke through resistance to finish at a new contract high.
"It's in uncharted territory," said a fund manager, adding that market sentiment remained bullish.
Another trader said most of the business was among market professionals, adding that he had not seen such a big move since 1993.
He cited expectations of lower European interest rates, but particularly in German, to explain the hectic activity.
"The market was flying away, obviously," he said.
